subject: refactor!: Flexible layout system. (#190)
body:
This is a huge refactor that gives the layout system in the views far
greater flexibility. The primary motivation behind this PR is the
planned merge-tool (#22) that is going to make use of 3-way diffs. I
want the conflicted files to appear in their own section in the normal
Diffview, thus the views need to be able to restructure the layout
dynamically depending on what entry is currently open. The previous
implementation was deeply tied to the 2-way diff layout, and it would be
unfeasible to force it to conform to a bodged dynamic layout system
without larger structural changes.

BREAKING CHANGES:

The only breaking change affects the action `view_windo`. This action is
not in use by default, so you won't be affected unless you know that
you've made use of it in your config.

Different entries in the same view may now use completely different
window layouts. Thus the action `view_windo` has changed to reflect
these changes. See `:h diffview-actions-view_windo` for more details on
the new usage.

subject: BREAKING CHANGE: Commit log panel and new config for panels (#136)
body:
* refactor: Move file tree stuff into 'ui'.

* feat: Implemented the commit log panel.

This implements a commit log panel that can be opened from both
diffviews and file history views. This will show the full commit
descriptions of all targeted commits. It can be configured to open
either as a floating window (default) or a normal split.

This commit also encompasses some major refactoring and extensions of
the 'Panel' class, which is the reason for the extensive list of changed
files.

Other changes:
- fix(file-history): The file history panel finally learned when not to
  use a plural 's'.
- fix(api): Fixed the order of execution of hooks in custom diffviews.

* feat(panel): Window scoped autocmds.

* break: Make 'file_panel' and 'file_history_panel' use 'win_config'

Other changes:
- docs: Document 'win_config'. Amend changelog.
- chore: Deprecation notices for old config.

* fix: Don't open log when comparing HEAD against uncommitted changes.

refactor!: change Package API
body:
This changes the following public APIs:

**(_breaking_) Events on the `Package` class**
The `uninstall:success` event on the `Package` class now receives an `InstallReceipt` as argument, instead of an
`InstallHandle`. This receipt is an in-memory representation of what was uninstalled. There's also a new
`uninstall:failed` event for situations where uninstallation for some
reason fails. Note: this also applies to the registry events (i.e.
`package:uninstall:success` and `package:uninstall:failed`).

---

**(_breaking_) `Package:uninstall()` is now asynchronous and receives two new arguments, similarly to `Package:install()`**
While package uninstallations remain synchronous under the hood, the public API has been changed from synchronous ->
asynchronous. Users of this method are recommended to provide a callback in situations where code needs to execute after
uninstallation fully completes.

---

**(_breaking_) `Package:get_install_path()` has been removed.

---

**`Package:install()` now takes an optional callback**
This callback allows consumers to be informed whether installation was successful or not without having to go through a
different, low-level, API. See below for a comparison between the old and new APIs:
```lua
-- before
local handle = pkg:install()
handle:once("closed", function ()
    -- ...
end)

-- after
pkg:install({}, function (success, result)
    -- ...
end)
```

body:
Move gitsigns.attach() to an opts-based API so bufnr, ctx, trigger, and
force can evolve without adding more positional arguments. Keep the old
public and low-level call shapes working so existing callers continue to
attach.

Use force to distinguish manual attaches from auto-attach triggers. This
lets attach({ force = true }) and :Gitsigns attach --force bypass the
attach_to_untracked and -diff checks, while plain :Gitsigns attach
continues to follow the normal auto-attach filters.

Regenerate the help docs, add @inlinedoc support so AttachOpts is
rendered inline, and document GitContext separately. Update the tests to
cover the new API and command-line manual attach behavior on -diff
buffers.

subject: fix: restore cursor position after auto-wrap (#2426)
body:
PR #2378 introduced a regression by using :startinsert! after :normal! gww.

startinsert! forces insert mode at the end of the line (similar to A in normal mode), which moves the cursor from its original position. As a result, the cursor would jump to the end of the line after auto-wrap.

Replaces it with :startinsert, which correctly restores insert mode at the previous insert position and preserves the cursor location.
